articles.headline: Premier League VAR review: Why no Man United penalty at Fulham?
articles.description: VAR often causes controversy, but how are decisions made? Our resident ref, Andy Davies, explains all.
articles.body:
The video assistant referee causes controversy every week, whether it be the Premier League, Champions League or FA Cup, but how are those decisions made and are they correct?

For the 2026-27 season, we are taking a look at the major incidents to explain the process in terms of both VAR protocol and the laws of the game. The most surprising, controversial and complicated decisions will be examined all season long right here.

 Andy Davies (@andydaviesref) is a former Select Group referee, with over 12 seasons on the elite list, working across the Premier League and Championship. With extensive experience at the elite level, he has operated within the VAR space in the Premier League and offers a unique insight into the processes, rationale and protocols that are delivered on a matchday. 

Should Man United have gotten a penalty at Fulham?

Fulham 1-1 Man United (Sept. 20)

Referee: Peter Bankes

VAR: Nick Hopton

Time: 86 minutes

Incident: Possible penalty to Man United for a handball

What happened: Man United's Lisandro Martínez felt he should have earned a penalty when he fired the ball at Fulham defender Calvin Bassey from close range and the ball struck Bassey's arm. The referee did not feel it was an offence and waved away the appeals for a penalty.

VAR decision: VAR agreed with the referee's interpretation of the incident, that the ball was struck at close range, defenders' arms were close to his body and within bodyline and therefore not a handball offence. VAR checked and cleared the on-filed decision as correct.

Verdict and insight: While Man United might have wanted the penalty, this was a correct on-field decision by the refereeing team and non-intervention by VAR.

This incident is a good example of how the handball law can create confusion in these types of situations. When the ball is struck at close range, the law is clear that the referee should allow play to continue if the player's hand or arm movement is the result of a natural reflex to potentially protect the player's face, and if such action does not make their body unnaturally bigger.

Additionally, if arms are within the body line and the ball would have struck the body/face this should also be taken into consideration when applying this law.

Bassey's reaction falls within this interpretation and was a good read by the on-field assistant referee, who would have led the communication in this incident.

Was Rice lucky not to be sent off at Brighton?

Brighton & Hove Albion 3-0 Arsenal (Sept. 19)

Referee: Darren England

VAR: Tim Wood

Time: 90 + 7 mins

Incident: Possible red card for Arsenal's Declan Rice

What happened: Rice picked up a late yellow card when he appeared to kick out at Brighton's Malick Yalcouyé in an off-the-ball incident.

VAR decision: The on-field decision of yellow card was checked and cleared as correct by the VAR.

articles.headline: Patriots starting RG Mike Onwenu carted off with ankle injury
articles.description: Patriots starting right guard Mike Onwenu was carted off the field with an ankle injury late in the first quarter of Sunday's game against the Steelers.
articles.body:
FOXBOROUGH, Mass. -- New England Patriots starting right guard Mike Onwenu was carted off the field late in the first quarter of Sunday's game against the Pittsburgh Steelers, and the team quickly ruled him out with a right ankle injury.

The injury came on a play when quarterback Drake Maye was sacked, and Steelers linebacker T.J. Watt landed on the back of Onwenu's legs.

Onwenu is a seven-year veteran who has the longest tenure with the Patriots after being selected in the sixth round of the 2020 draft.

Durability has been one of his calling cards, as Sunday marked his 100th career regular-season game and 92nd start. A University of Michigan alum, he also has played in five playoff games (four starts).

Onwenu, 28, is in the final year of his contract in 2026.

Veteran Greg Van Roten, whom the Patriots signed to a one-year, $3 million deal on Aug. 18, took over for Onwenu.

articles.headline: Rangers put pitcher Quantrill on IL due to right lat tightness
articles.description: The Rangers put versatile right-hander Cal Quantrill on the 15-day injured list Sunday, a day after he exited following only four batters and 12 pitches because of right lat tightness.
articles.body:
ARLINGTON, Texas -- The AL West-leading Texas Rangers put versatile right-hander Cal Quantrill on the 15-day injured list Sunday, a day after he exited following only four batters and 12 pitches because of right lat tightness.

Hard-throwing right-hander Winston Santos was recalled from Triple-A Round Rock and joined the Rangers before the finale of their three-game series against Toronto.

About an hour before the game, the Rangers said right fielder Brandon Nimmo was being scratched from the starting lineup because of illness.

Before the IL move was announced, manager Skip Schumaker said the Rangers knew going into Saturday night's game that Quantrill's velocity was lower.

Quantrill (9-5) was showing no signs of pain when Schumaker, pitching coach Jordan Tiegs and head trainer Matt Lucero went to the mound in the second inning and he came out of the game. Quantrill has a 2.86 ERA in 32 games (15 starts) after going to spring training with the Rangers on a minor league deal.

He left his previous start after six innings and 70 pitches at Arizona last Sunday with back soreness.

Quantrill, 31, has a 1.75 ERA (11 earned runs in 56⅔ innings) over his past 11 appearances (10 starts). Cam Schlittler of the New York Yankees at 1.64 is the only qualified pitcher with a better ERA over that span.

Santos is beginning his third stint with the Rangers, though his only appearance in the first two was his big league debut on July 1 at Cleveland, where he allowed two runs in two innings. He has 103 strikeouts in 83⅓ innings in the minor leagues this season.

articles.headline: Has Isak finally found form at Liverpool? Winner at Bournemouth gives Iraola hope
articles.description: Liverpool's expensively assembled attack had looked devoid of a spark at Bournemouth, with Alexander Isak virtually anonymous ... until he wasn't.
articles.body:
BOURNEMOUTH, England -- As Liverpool striker Alexander Isak watched his mishit cross veer erratically out of play at AFC Bournemouth's Vitality Stadium, ironic jeers rained down on him from the stands.

Minutes later, the Sweden international was the subject of adulation -- not ire -- from the away section of the crowd after netting what turned out to be the winning goal in his side's hard-fought 1-0 Premier League victory Sunday.

- First-month grades for all 20 Premier League teams: From an A+ to F

- Ranking the hottest men's teams right now: Can anyone stop Barcelona?

The sequence was a microcosm of the life of a striker and a timely reminder of why the Reds broke the British transfer record to sign Isak from Newcastle United little more than 12 months ago.

Up until that point, it had largely been a drab, laborious slog for Andoni Iraola's side on their head coach's return to his former club. The Reds' expensively assembled attack had looked devoid of a spark, with Isak virtually anonymous at the Vitality Stadium ... until he wasn't.

With the clock ticking toward the hour mark, Cody Gakpo's cross bobbled into the path of the forward, who finished with aplomb before charging toward the elated away end. The hearty embrace he received from the visiting supporters felt symbolic. After the most turbulent of debut seasons, there can now be no doubting that Isak is a Liverpool player.

"A striker's job is like this," Iraola said in his postmatch news conference. "He had a couple of crosses that he did not hit properly or control but in the end he has to help us to be closer to the box, to play in the opposition's half and have more meaningful possession. And then if the team is playing there, he will receive rewards in terms of goals."

Indeed, Isak's tally of four Premier League goals has already exceeded his haul from the entirety of last term (three). In the 81 minutes he played against Bournemouth, the 26-year-old had 34 touches and completed just 11 of his 16 attempted passes. Ultimately, though, it is immaterial what he does outside of the penalty area if he can continue showing the kind of proficiency that has characterized the early weeks of his season.

Of course, the fact that Isak was given the platform to go on and win the game owed much to the robustness of Liverpool's defense. For the first time since the beginning of Arne Slot's tenure in August and September 2024, the Reds have kept three consecutive clean sheets in the Premier League, with summer signing Jérémy Jacquet impressing once again on the south coast.

At the end of a week that saw him earn his first senior callup to the France national team, the 21-year-old continued his outstanding start at the heart of Liverpool's back line. articles.headline: José Mourinho blasts ref, VAR: 'Two clear red cards' for Atlético Madrid
articles.description: José Mourinho blasted the referee and the VAR after Real Madrid's 2-1 derby defeat to Atlético Madrid, saying Atlético should have received "two clear red cards."
articles.body:
José Mourinho blasted the referee and the VAR after Real Madrid's 2-1 derby defeat to Atlético Madrid, saying Atlético should have received "two clear red cards" and claiming the on-field official "couldn't cope with the pressure."

Alejandro Grimaldo put Atlético ahead with a second-half penalty at the Metropolitano -- after defender Dean Huijsen was sent off for bringing down Giuliano Simeone -- before Jonathan David made it 2-0. Antonio Rüdiger pulled a late goal back as Madrid dropped to fourth in the LaLiga table.

However, Mourinho's post-match news conference focused on two first-half incidents, where Atlético's Cristian Romero was shown a yellow card -- not a red -- for treading on Jude Bellingham's knee, while Lee Kang-in escaped punishment for a crunching challenge on Federico Valverde.

Mourinho brought printed-out photos of the two incidents into the press room to show journalists, before delivering a long, damning indictment of referee Miguel Ángel Ortiz Arias and VAR Daniel Trujillo Suárez.

"The story of the game is here," Mourinho said, holding up the images of the two challenges. "They're two clear red cards. With the difficulties we had afterwards -- with 11 versus 10 [players] -- you could imagine what it would have been like [for us] for 50 minutes with 11 versus nine.

"It's the CTA [the referee's committee]. It's all been very strange. It's a referee [Ortiz Arias] who, at 41, doesn't have international experience. I don't know why he was the referee. The poor guy came here and couldn't cope with the pressure.

"But for [the VAR] there's no pressure, at [RFEF HQ] Las Rozas there's no pressure. Or maybe there is and we don't know... That combination -- a poor referee, who's only done small games, and a VAR with a big history. Congratulations to the CTA."

The Portuguese coach said he hadn't yet seen a replay of Huijsen's red card, and went on to list a series of incidents in games involving Real Madrid, Barcelona and Atlético in recent weeks, suggesting Real's rivals had benefitted.

"The penalty at Real Sociedad [for Atlético] is laughable," Mourinho said. "The penalty for Barcelona is laughable, the non-sending off [for Barcelona] against Athletic Club. So many things together... I thought I'd find a different league to the one I left [in 2013], and people told me no, and they explained why. But we'll fight."

Madrid are now six points behind leaders Barcelona with seven games played, going into the international break.

"If 'they' leave us in peace, and let us compete on an even playing field, there's a long way left," Mourinho said, when asked if his team could still fight for the title.

"I don't want to say this was prepared. I want to think they're mistakes, like a coach makes mistakes. I want to think the CTA made a mistake, and picked a referee of 41, who's never been in this situation. They made a mistake, that's all."

articles.headline: Packers WR Reed, RT Bako-Bewele carted off with injuries
articles.description: Packers wide receiver Jayden Reed and right tackle Zach Bako-Bewele were carted off the field on back-to-back plays Sunday.
articles.body:
EAST RUTHERFORD, N.J. -- Green Bay Packers receiver Jayden Reed was carted off the field after being placed on a stabilizing backboard with a neck injury following the second play from scrimmage in Sunday's game against the New York Jets at MetLife Stadium.

On the very next play, Packers right tackle Zach Bako-Bewele sustained a right knee injury and also was carted off the field. Bako-Bewele's leg was immediately placed in a cast before he got on the cart.

Both players were quickly ruled out for the game by the Packers.

Members of the medical staff from both teams attended to Reed for several minutes on the field before he was placed on a board and had his helmet strapped down for stabilization.

Reed took what appeared to be a hit in the head and neck area at the end of a 4-yard gain on a swing pass in the left flat. Jets linebacker Demario Davis was the initial defender to hit Reed, and then Kingsley Enagbare also may have made contact with Reed after that.

Players from both teams took a knee while Reed was down.

articles.headline: Man United rescue draw at Fulham after own goal shocker
articles.description: A comical own goal by Lisandro Martinez saw Manchester United fail to win for a third Premier League game in a row as they drew 1-1 with Fulham at Craven Cottage.
articles.body:
A comical own goal by Lisandro Martínez saw Manchester United fail to win for a third Premier League game in a row as they drew 1-1 with Fulham at Craven Cottage.

It was a lethargic, muted display from Michael Carrick's side, who will spend the international break in the bottom half of the Premier League table, though they were spared from making it three losses in a week by Matheus Cunha's late deflected goal.

Their malaise was summed up by the surreal nature of the goal they gifted Fulham.

It went down against Martinez's name but the blame was shared with his goalkeeper, a botched effort by Senne Lammens to shovel away Calvin Bassey's shot with his legs rather than his gloves, then an equally inexplicable and muddled attempt at keeping the defender's pass back to him out of his net.

Cunha too had been at fault, crumpling into a heap in midfield and allowing Bassey to sprint the ball away, though the Brazilian would redeem himself, rescuing his side in the 89th minute with a shot that deflected heavily off David Affengruber.

There could be little arguing United deserved anything more than they got, indeed Fulham ought to have given Alvaro Arbeloa his first Premier League win.

There was plenty here to offer the Spaniard encouragement. Early on, Antonee Robinson moved the ball inside to Gonzalo García who shot wide in search of his second Premier League goal. Martinez hit a thunderous effort from range that needed turning away at full-stretch by Bernd Leno.

The game had been played at a sedentary, almost pre-season pace but burst suddenly into life midway through the half.

United came within inches of going ahead when Cunha got the better of Affengruber near the byline and cut back for Bruno Fernandes to roll a shot against a post.

Lammens, prior to his second-half howler, made three saves in quick succession, the best of them a smart block from Sander Berge. Oscar Bobb then dragged wide from a good position before Leno was needed again to tip away Cunha's awkward deflected effort.

The United goalkeeper had a perplexing afternoon. At times he was keeping his team in it, sticking out a boot to divert Josh King's low shot behind, then later racing from goal to smother as Alex Iwobi went through.

A lovely turn and cross by Cunha found Marcus Rashford, arguably still not looking at ease back at United, who leaned back and leathered his effort into the Fulham supporters behind the goal.

United got themselves into a horrible mess for Fulham's goal. Cunha made a feeble attempt to keep the ball from Bassey, who put the Brazilian on the floor and raced into the box. His shot was tame and straight at Lammens who made the strange decision to bounce away with his thigh, then could not recover as Martinez's pass back to him squirmed into the corner.

Bryan Mbeumo was denied by a flying save from Leno, who also kept out Cunha's curling effort as it bent towards the bottom corner.

articles.headline: Phillies option Orion Kerkering to Triple-A, call up Max Lazar
articles.description: The Phillies optioned reliever Orion Kerkering to Triple-A Lehigh Valley after he posted an 18.69 ERA in his four appearances this month.
articles.body:
NEW YORK -- The Philadelphia Phillies optioned reliever Orion Kerkering to Triple-A Lehigh Valley on Sunday after he posted an 18.69 ERA in his four appearances this month.

The right-hander gave up four runs in the eighth inning of Saturday's 10-3 loss to the New York Mets, after which interim manager Don Mattingly admitted he was concerned about the 25-year-old and uncertain where he could continue using him.

"You have to be able to use him there in a game like that," Mattingly said. "Not going to try to chase a three-run deficit in that inning. It's hard to find places to use him."

Kerkering established himself as one of the Phillies' most reliable setup men by going 13-7 with a 2.78 ERA and four saves over the previous two seasons. But he committed a season-ending throwing error in the 11th inning of Game 4 of the 2025 National League Division Series, when he tossed the ball over the head of catcher J.T. Realmuto trying to force out Hyeseong Kim, who scored the winning run in the Los Angeles Dodgers' 2-1 victory.

Kerkering opened this season with a 2.03 ERA in his first 29 appearances and still had an ERA below 3.00 through July 28. He is 1-1 with a 10.80 ERA and one save in his last 19 appearances.

To replace Kerkering on the active roster, the Phillies promoted right-hander Max Lazar from Lehigh Valley.
